To depict (something) in a way which can be seen.
d.x: to visualize data using a chart

d.g: To form a mental picture of (something); to picture (something) in the mind; to envisage.
d.x: In our own poetry we get from [Geoffrey] Chaucer the first instance of self-analysis and description, the first case of visualising self.

d.g: To make (a hidden or unclear body part, process, or object) visible by optical methods (such as endoscopy, magnetic resonance imaging, ultrasound, or X-rays), or other techniques.

visualize.e: From visual + -ize (suffix forming verbs denoting the doing or making of what is denoted by the adjectives or nouns to which it is attached).

d.g: To give life to something; to animate.
